chapter: Ellington band members and life on the road
title: Johnny Hodges, chicken and his straight face
summary: Bigard and Willard recall Hodges cooking and eating chicken and corn on the cob, and how his straight face hid his humor.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, at the Vine Lodge or the Players?
Yeah, he was cooking for -- he was doing -- he's cooking chicken for --
Well, Johnny always found a place to find some chicken. And I remember when he used to come to Los Angeles to go to the Park Hotel and get a big jar of greens and chicken --
-- and he'd bring it back to Hollywood. He wanted to live in Hollywood but he wanted to eat off Central Avenue.
And sometimes he would cook where he was and sometimes he would just go out and buy fried chicken somewhere. But Johnny loved chicken, I know. (Unintelligible.) Wings and gizzard.
Yeah. And he loved corn on the cob. Boy, he loves that.
If you didn't know Johnny, you wouldn't know how to take him, -- I know, that's right. (Inaudible.)
-- because he's so -- he's always got a straight face, you know. I mean, looked like it hurted him to laugh.
He didn't look like he sounded.
